nodes.label: Repository Architecture Overview
nodes.rationale: Facade-based architecture separates loader/predictor/integrations from src/timesfm_app internals so the app.py entrypoint depends on stable public contracts rather than internal modules.

nodes.label: SSRF-Hardened URL Resolver
nodes.rationale: Remote files are untrusted: resolver allows only HTTP/S, revalidates redirects, blocks private/special-purpose IP ranges, caps downloads at 200 MiB, and checks extensions/binary signatures because compressed formats can expand significantly in local memory.

nodes.label: Patching (Input/Output Patch Mechanism)
nodes.rationale: Passing every scalar as a separate transformer token would make long histories expensive, so TimesFM groups consecutive observations into 32-point input patches and 128-point output patches, trading per-token granularity for tractable long-context compute.

nodes.label: TimesFM 2.5 Frequency Indicator Removal
nodes.rationale: TimesFM 2.5 removed the frequency indicator from its API; in this app, frequency only validates the historical grid and generates future timestamps rather than being passed to the model, so seasonal behavior must be present in the numeric context itself.

nodes.label: uv Setup (Recommended Environment Method)
nodes.rationale: uv is recommended over venv/Conda because it reads project metadata, installs a compatible Python, and reproduces the exact locked dependency set including the pinned CUDA 13.0 PyTorch index, which requirements.txt-based paths cannot encode.

nodes.label: Loading a Public URL (Untrusted Remote Resolver)
nodes.rationale: The resolver deliberately treats remote files as untrusted: HTTP/S-only allowlist, no embedded credentials, DNS/IP validation blocking private/loopback/link-local ranges, redirect revalidation, a 200 MiB streaming limit, and extension/signature checks, because format validation alone cannot bound decompressed workbook or Parquet memory.

nodes.label: Linear Interpolation Mathematics for Internal Gaps
nodes.rationale: Internal target gaps are preserved and counted rather than silently filled, because both neighboring values can anchor a defensible linear interpolation, whereas leading gaps have no left anchor and trailing gaps leave the forecast origin ambiguous - so those are trimmed/rejected instead.
nodes.norm_label: linear interpolation mathematics for internal gaps

nodes.label: Dimension Matching and Compilation Buckets (32/128-point rounding)
nodes.rationale: The app rounds requested context up to the nearest 32 and horizon up to the nearest 128 to match TimesFM's patch boundaries, and enforces compiled context + compiled horizon <= 16384; because horizon 1 still compiles to 128, the UI caps selectable context at 16256 to keep the combined limit satisfiable.
nodes.norm_label: dimension matching and compilation buckets (32/128-point rounding)
